parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has a single file, OrdersController. It handles one concern: the HTTP endpoints for the Orders aggregate (create, read, item management and lifecycle transitions). Each handler only maps HTTP params and body to an application call. There is no business logic, validation or invariant here, so nothing is duplicated from the application or domain layers. Reads always go through QueryBus with GetOrderQuery and GetOrdersQuery. Writes always go through the injected *Service.execute calls. This is a mix of a bus for queries and direct services for commands, but each side follows its own approach every time. That reads as a deliberate CQRS-lite split, not a bypass of an abstraction, so I didn't count it as a violation. It is still worth checking that the application layer doesn't also offer a CommandBus path for these operations. The controller doesn't skip the application layer to reach repositories or domain entities.
